usual_baseline: Follow-up endoscopy is both late and misdirected. Only 23% were scoped within the 8-week target [2081], and 1 of 21 within 6–8 weeks [2774]. Many uncomplicated cases are scoped without need: 78.9% [2532], 42/55 without an indication [2748], 27 unnecessary cases [2868]. Yet 39% with an indication had no endoscopy [2748]. Hinchey score was recorded in 8.7% [2868].
fix_that_works: Staff training and awareness raised timely colonoscopy in complicated cases from 5% to 46% [2774]. Targeted teaching and posters raised appropriate endoscopy booking from 60% to 71% [2812]. Without a stated intervention, flexible sigmoidoscopy in uncomplicated cases fell from 48.8% to 29.4% [2226].
fix_that_fails: No intervention was followed by no improvement. Timeliness stayed poor: after staff training, only 6 of 18 complicated cases had timely colonoscopy [2774]. After teaching and posters, 29% of eligible patients still had no endoscopy booked [2812].
consultant_advice: The yield in uncomplicated disease is low: no cancer in 82 colonoscopies [2532], no malignancy in the over-investigated group [2868], and £35,202 spent on unindicated scopes [2748]. Audit whether complicated cases get timely scoping and whether uncomplicated cases are spared it. Record CT staging so the indication can be judged.
